name: Pickleball / racquet club
summary: Indoor (or covered) pickleball club: clear-span building (often pre-engineered metal or a converted big box) with ~2,500–3,500 gross SF per court including lobby, pro shop, restrooms/lockers and a small F&B bar. Outdoor municipal court bids ($61k–$172k per court, amenities block) set the floor for court-only work; indoor cost is derived from RSMeans racquetball/gym $/SF × SF per court. Three 2024–25 indoor projects give $154k (TX, pickleball-only), $367k (FL municipal contract) and $800k (FL premium club) per court; RSMeans racquetball/gym models cross-check $/SF.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: e5 ≈ 2,230 SF per court (29,000 SF / 13 courts, pickleball-only); e3 4,000 SF per court (100,000 SF / 25 courts with wellness/coworking/restaurant). Gross building SF per court: recommended court playing area ~30x60 ft (1,800 SF) for one court plus spectator/circulation, lobby, pro shop, restrooms/lockers and F&B (~25–50% add). Derived.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Building at ~0.25–0.35 FAR with surface parking ≈ 11,000–15,000 SF building/acre ÷ 2,800 SF/court ≈ 4–6 courts/acre (higher in reused big boxes). Derived.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: 4 players per court plus waiting/social players and staff ≈ 5–8 spaces per court. Derived.

perPrimaryUnit.method: 2025 dollars. Sourced per-court points: Live Oak TX $154k (2024 TDLR estimate, pickleball-only, ~$69/SF, e5); Palmetto Bay FL $367k (2025 municipal construction contract with shop and bar, e4); Boca Raton FL $800k (2025, premium club with padel, wellness, restaurant; likely project cost, e3). Mid $400k ≈ e4 adjusted up slightly for national sitework/parking and to sit between e5 and e3; cross-check perSF $145 × 2,800 SF/court ≈ $405k, consistent with RSMeans 2019 racquetball club $172/SF union / $155 open shop (e1) escalated. Low = e5-type simple building/conversion; high = e3 premium club. Outdoor court-only bids ($61k–$172k per court, amenities e9–e11) are the floor.

perSF.method: Low ≈ e5 $69/SF (simple pickleball-only building, 2024); mid = perPrimaryUnit mid / 2,800 SF per court; high ≈ e3 $200/SF (2025 premium club) and RSMeans masonry club (e1 ≈ $172/SF 2019 → ~$225 2025) plus premium F&B finishes.

scope.notes: Building + court surfaces/nets + typical on-site work (parking, utilities, landscaping). Excludes land, soft costs, FF&E (furniture, ball machines, pro-shop fixtures), off-sites, impact/tap fees.

qualityTiers.method: economy ≈ low/mid (150/400 ≈ 0.38, e5-type); luxury = high/mid (800/400 = 2.0, e3-type); premium interpolated.

systemSplit.method: Derived for a pre-engineered metal building club: the PEMB package sits in 13 (≈18%); slab and foundations 03; court surfacing/finishes split 09; HVAC 10% (conditioned play halls); lighting/power 8%; on-site work 12%. Not sourced from a published estimate.

lineItems.name: Indoor court surfacing (acrylic or cushioned), lines, posts and nets

cost.method: Derived allowance per court on an existing slab; cushioned or modular tile systems at the high end.

lineItems.name: Outdoor post-tension pickleball court (fenced)

cost.method: Amenities block pickleball-court-outdoor: municipal bids $61k (Troy MI), $95k (Farragut TN), $172k (Tuscaloosa AL) per court.

lineItems.notes: Optional outdoor courts beside the club.

cost.method: Derived allowance per outdoor court for poles, fixtures and controls.
Derived allowance for bar, small kitchen, hood where cooked food is served.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Lounge furniture, benches, ball machines, scoring/video systems, pro shop fixtures per court. Derived.

pctOfHard.method: Simple PEMB buildings carry lower A&E (~5–7%; RSMeans model shows ~7–8% architectural fees, e1) plus civil, permits, testing → 10–22%. Derived.

softCosts.notes: Conversions of big boxes need change-of-use permitting and often HVAC/sprinkler upgrades.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Covered outdoor/converted (~$150k hard × 1.1 soft, less margin) to premium ground-up ($800k × 1.25).

source.title: Racquetball Court - Commercial Construction Costs Per Square Foot (RSMeans model page)

evidence.quote: Racquetball Court with Brick Veneer / Rigid Steel ... SubTotal 100% $137.52 ... Contractor Fees (General Conditions,Overhead,Profit) 25% $34.38
evidence.scopeNotes: 2019 RSMeans national model, 30,000 SF, 2 story, union labor. value = subtotal + 25% contractor fees = $171.9/SF; open shop = $155.06/SF. Building only: excludes the architectural fees (6–8%) shown on the page, sitework, FF&E. Indoor racquet club proxy (2-story model with courts, lockers, lobby).

source.title: Construction Begins on Florida’s $20 Million Indoor Pickleball Complex

evidence.quote: Boca Paddle by CityPickle, a $20 million, 100,000-square-foot indoor pickleball and padel complex in Boca Raton. The public-private partnership project will include 25 courts, wellness spaces, coworking areas, cold plunges, saunas, and a restaurant.
evidence.scopeNotes: Premium club with padel, wellness and restaurant; $20M / 25 courts ≈ $800k per court, ≈ $200/SF; likely project cost (scope of $20M not itemized). June 2025.

source.title: Indoor pickleball courts in Palmetto Bay could be completed by November

evidence.quote: may host nine courts, a sports shop, and a bar serving drinks and food ... The council awarded the $3.3 million construction contract to Waypoint Contracting.
evidence.scopeNotes: Municipal new-build indoor facility on a 2+ acre lot; construction contract (hard cost) $3.3M / 9 courts ≈ $367k per court. Land ($2.94M) excluded. Contract awarded July 2025.

source.title: Indoor pickleball complex planned for North San Antonio suburb of Live Oak

evidence.quote: The nearly 29,000-square-foot complex at 201 Shin Oak Drive will house 12 indoor courts and one outdoor stadium court, according to a Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation filing ... Construction of the space is projected to cost $2 million
evidence.scopeNotes: TDLR-filed construction estimate; pickleball-only (no restaurant). $2M / 13 courts ≈ $154k per court; ≈ $69/SF; ≈ 2,230 SF per court. May 2024.

openQuestions: More indoor club budgets outside Florida/Texas would firm up the national mid; e3 cost scope (hard vs. total) is unclear.
Confirm gross SF per court for clubs with significant F&B.
